hypothesis_text: Acute 30-minute liquidation imbalances exceeding |0.6| on midcap altcoins (SOL, BNB, XRP) induce temporary price overshooting driven by mechanical margin-call liquidations. Upon cessation of forced liquidating flow, the market undergoes an exhaustion mean-reversion rebound over 1h to 4h horizons, which is further sharpened in states of extreme order book depth imbalance, aggressive taker exhaustion, and heightened Garman-Klass intraday volatility.
narrative: When leveraged positions breach maintenance margin on cryptocurrency perpetual futures, exchanges execute automated market orders to liquidate the collateral. During an acute cascade where liquidation_imbalance_30m exceeds |0.6|, forced orders heavily skew to one side (e.g. forced selling from long liquidations when imbalance > 0, or forced buying from short liquidations when imbalance < 0). This forced non-discretionary flow rapidly consumes resting liquidity across multiple order book levels, causing temporary price dislocation away from fundamental equilibrium. Because liquidation orders are purely mechanical and price-insensitive, they terminate abruptly once margin requirements are satisfied. The sudden withdrawal of forced liquidating flow creates an immediate order flow vacuum. Opportunistic market makers and contrarian liquidity providers step in to rebuild the order book, absorbing remaining inventory at favorable prices and driving an exhaustion mean-reversion snapback over the subsequent 1h to 4h. The rebound is conditioned by three distinct market microstructure roles: (1) Order book depth imbalance (depth_imbalance_10): resting depth on the opposite side serves as an absorption barrier that limits cascade depth and anchors the pivot point; (2) Taker buy ratio (taker_buy_ratio_1h): aggressive taker volume climax marks the peak of capitulation after which aggressor momentum depletes; and (3) Garman-Klass volatility (volatility_garman_klass_1h): extreme intra-bar dispersion reflects heightened liquidity distress and overshooting, expanding the magnitude of the subsequent mean-reversion rebound.
research_rationale: The anchor candidate XL_midcap_alt_4ad50c938ba4 isolates acute liquidation imbalances (|liquidation_imbalance_30m| > 0.6) across the midcap_alt basket (SOL, BNB, XRP) on 15m bars, capturing 16,467 bars (13.3% match rate) across 413 active days and 413 independent events. Per liquidation_provenance, 6,140 matched bars occur during the observed exchange liquidation feed (58.7% match rate across 38 of 38 observed days), while 10,327 bars sit in the historical estimated OHLCV period. In the T1 window, 242-246 days per symbol feature observed liquidation feeds. Historical cemetery evidence for liquidation_imbalance_30m reveals 874 trials with a dominant kill code of T0.04-IC-STAT (706 trials), indicating that continuous unconditioned formulas fail because liquidation signals are absent on over 81% of ordinary bars, diluting continuous IC. Our locked candidate solves this by restricting signal activation strictly to acute cascade events (|imbalance| > 0.6). For composition, we incorporate three motivated microstructure partners admitted via probe_partner (coverage = 1.0): (1) depth_imbalance_10 (gate_tail) provides resting depth asymmetry (|z| > 2) with 485 projected T1 event observations; (2) taker_buy_ratio_1h (gate_tail) captures aggressor flow climax (|z| > 2) with 260 projected T1 event observations; (3) volatility_garman_klass_1h (gate_tail) identifies extreme volatility regimes (|z| > 2) with 890 projected T1 event observations. While funding_rate_zscore_30d was also probed, its gates fell short of the 250 T1 event observation floor (projected observations < 250) and were excluded. Search scope full is selected to allow the Layer 2.5 mutator and automatic grid to explore couplings among these motivated partners while appropriately deflating DSR.
